newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA 1997 SUGAR PRODUCTION SEEN RISING.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA 1997 SUGAR PRODUCTION SEEN RISING.

text.p: Bulgaria's production of white sugar from sugar beet is seen rising to 10,000 tonnes this year from 5,100 tonnes last year, the Union of Sugar Producers said on Friday.

"Sugar production from sugar beet this year will rise to 10,000 tonnes this year from 5,100 last year but down from 14,700 tonnes in 1995 because of the favourable weather this spring," the Union's chairman, Boris Tersiev, told a news conference.
Bulgaria's domestic sugar consumption stood at 26 kg per capita anually in 1996, National Statistics Institute figures showed. Annual consumption is forecast to rise to 33 kg per capita by 2001.
Bulgaria meets its consumption needs mainly by importing sugar cane from South America, which is processed in the country's six sugar processing plants.
"Total (cane plus beet) white sugar production last year amounted to 297,500 tonnes, up from 274,000 tonnes in 1995," Tersiev said.
Cheap labour allows a lot of companies to import sugar cane and export white sugar to neighbouring countries.
"Bulgaria exported 131,000 tonnes of white sugar to Macedonia, Albania, Greece and Turkey (in 1996), up from 112,000 tonnes in 1995 and 66,000 tonnes in 1994," Tersiev said.
"A further 19,000 tonnes of white sugar were exported in the first quarter of this year," he added.
Bulgaria's cabinet scrapped price controls on sugar last month in line with pledges to the International Monetary Fund to liberalise trade in agricultural goods.

"Sugar producers are not optimistic about the development of this industry in the future because of low local retail price of some $0.40-0.45 per kilogramme of white sugar and a farm gate price which was set by the cabinet at $20 per tonne of sugar beet," Tersiev said.

"We hope that Bulgaria's integration in the Central European Free Trade Association and in the European Union will boost sugar beet production under the EU common agricultural policy," he said. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 4145
